title: Mid-sprint Bridge Notes — Serving Runtime / Infra / Console
content:
Context
- Mid-sprint bridge to align serving-runtime, infra, and console teams on rollouts and optics. Short, focused (30m) sync, followed by async action-tracking.
- Primary goals: unblock rollout of v0.21 kernel selection, confirm canary metrics, and finalize console telemetry surface for batching suggestions.

Logistics
- When: Fri 2026-03-13 09:30-10:00 PT (30m)
- Attendees (invite): Priya (runtime PM), Diego (infra lead), Maya (console PM), Arjun (SRE), Lin (QA), me (Oliver)
- Slack bridge: #serving-bridge (use thread for quick notes)

Meeting goals (3)
1) Quick health check: canary SLOs from infra + runtime telemetry. Are we green for broader rollout?
2) Action triage: who owns immediate infra/kernel patches and console telemetry mapping?
3) Risk & rollback plan sanity-check: confirm fallback model variant mapping and operator runbook updates.

Agenda (tight timeline)
- 0-5m: Quick updates (one-liners) — Priya (runtime status), Diego (infra capacity), Maya (console UX changes)
- 5-15m: Canary metrics review (Arjun + Lin) — latency p50/p95, error rate, CPU/GPU saturations. Highlight anomalies since Tues.
- 15-22m: Rollout blockers & patch plan — review RI-4123, PR-987 status, infra hotfix timing.
- 22-28m: Console telemetry completion — mapping batching fields to UI labels; confirm names and sample payloads.
- 28-30m: Quick assignment of action items + next check-in cadence.

Pre-reads (please skim before meeting)
- RI-4123: kernel selection failing on mixed-precision workloads (ticket)
- PR 987: runtime patch for KV-cache eviction (WIP)
- Console draft: /confluence/Serving+Runtime+Rollout+Plan (section: telemetry-to-ui mapping)

Quick notes / my thoughts to surface
- Observed a small spike in p95 for requests with seq_len > 1024 on canary — suspect kernel fallback is thrashing. (note: check PR987 perf tests)
- Infra reported two preemption events on the dedicated pool Wed night. Need to confirm autoscaler cooldown settings are sane for canary.
- Console labels: prefer human-friendly wording for "prefix_cache_hit_rate" -> "Prompt cache hit %" (Maya to confirm).

Known blockers (short list)
- QA acceptance: lin needs deterministic repro for one flaky e2e — blocking full canary progression. (ticket: RI-4188)
- Infra: autoscaler cooldown may be too aggressive, causing transient capacity drops (Diego investigating).
- Runtime: PR987 failing on Windows runners in CI (non-blocking for rollout but noisy).

Decision points we need this meeting
- Proceed with canary to 20% or hold until Lin repro is resolved?
- Approve naming for console telemetry (final by Maya)
- Schedule for infra hotfix: now (risk brief) or post-weekend?

Action items (capture below — I'll push to the ticket after meeting)
- Oliver: compile concise meeting notes + assign Jira subtasks for each action (due 2026-03-16).
- Priya: coordinate with Lin to prioritize deterministic repro; if not found, prepare a rollback gating step (due 2026-03-14).
- Diego: present autoscaler cooldown telemetry and propose new cooldown values; plan hotfix window (due 2026-03-15).
- Maya: finalize console telemetry labels and provide sample UI mock for batching suggestions (due 2026-03-17).
- Arjun: run stress run on canary config focused on seq_len>1024 and share logs (due 2026-03-14).
- Lin: confirm acceptance tests and add a deterministic test case for the observed failure (link to RI-4188) (due 2026-03-15).

Follow-ups from last bridge (status)
- Diego: infra autoscaler tuning (was "in progress") — reported partial change made Tue; still observing preemptions (status: in_progress).
- Priya: runtime fallback metrics dashboard — initial dashboard pushed, needs retention increased (status: needs_followup).
- Maya: console batching UX prototype — shared, waiting on final labels (status: awaiting_decision).

Notes to self (Oliver)
- Bring up: need clearer SLO definition for canary (is it absolute p95 or delta vs baseline?). Recommend delta-based gating to avoid noisy flaps.
- Remind Priya to attach canary runbook to the rollout Confluence page if we approve expansion.
- If we delay rollout, propose a small internal canary with internal traffic only (no external customers) to reduce risk.

Risk matrix (very quick)
- High: autoscaler-driven capacity loss during rollout -> customer-facing errors. Mitigation: rollback + standby capacity + manual scale-on-call.
- Medium: telemetry mismatch in console -> confusion for customers using batching suggestions. Mitigation: clear UIs + tooltips + release note.
- Low: PR CI flakes -> delays in merge but not immediate user impact.

Meeting outputs I will produce
- Short meeting notes with action-item assignments + links to created subtasks (will update linked_artifacts).
- One-pager for SRE runbook adjustment if we widen the canary.

Questions I want to ask in the meeting
- Diego: can we temporarily pin canary to a dedicated small pool to avoid preemptions?
- Lin: how long do you need to add the deterministic test? Blocker or quick win?
- Maya: will the telemetry name change impact existing saved dashboards?

Misc scratch items (if time)
- Quick sketch: add a small "canary health" badge in the Console top bar (green/amber/red) + tooltip linking to canary dashboard. Good quick UX to reduce noise.
- Consider a weekly automated note that summarizes canary deltas for the product channel.

End of notes.
